subject: Clarification on notification obligations & subprocessor evidence transfer
messages:
From: Michael Reynolds <m.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Possible data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence transfer

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

We detected anomalous access patterns involving patient metadata in our integration logs and wanted to confirm Redwood's obligations under our DPA. Can you confirm:

- The notification window Redwood commits to after confirming a security incident that affects Acme Health
- Whether logs/forensic artifacts can be exported to our SFTP and expected timelines for transfer (we're under a 72-hour regulator request deadline)
- Any involvement of subprocessors (cloud provider, analytics vendor) that might affect evidence collection

We appreciate a quick confirmation. I can schedule a call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Michael Reynolds
Head of InfoSec, Acme Health Systems
security@acmehealth.com

Attachment: suspicious_access_snapshot.csv (csv, 14 KB)

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Michael Reynolds <m.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence transfer

Hi Michael — thanks for flagging and for the snapshot. Quick answers below; we'll follow up with a forensic summary by EOD tomorrow and can set up a call.

- Notification window: Our standard DPA (Section 4) commits to "prompt" notification and to provide initial incident notice within 48 hours of verification. For regulated customers we have an expedited workflow and targeted SLO of 24–48 hours for initial notice.

- Evidence transfer: We can export logs and forensic artifacts. For a full export to customer-managed SFTP we typically provide a secure export within 48–72 hours after we complete initial triage and embargo checks. If there are legal holds or third-party subprocessors involved, timelines can extend — we will surface those immediately.

- Subprocessors: We rely on two subprocessors for storage and metrics (CloudZone Inc. and Querylytics). Both are listed in our DPA subprocessor appendix. When evidence touches those services we coordinate retrieval with their SOC teams; that typically adds 6–24 hours depending on the artifact type.

Next steps: I'm attaching a short forensic summary template and our current DPA redline for the notification section (highlights on Section 4). Can Marissa loop Legal if we need DocuSign for any temporary access agreement? Aditya — can you confirm whether CloudZone logs for the window Michael sent are already available for export?

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: forensic_summary_template.pdf (pdf, 28 KB); dpa_section4_redlines.docx

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Michael Reynolds <m.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence transfer

On Jun 1, 2028, at 11:04 AM, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai wrote:
> Can Marissa loop Legal if we need DocuSign for any temporary access agreement? Aditya — can you confirm whether CloudZone logs for the window Michael sent are already available for export?

Confirmed — CloudZone retains the relevant request logs and KV cache snapshots for 30 days and we've already pulled the partition that covers the timestamp in Michael's snapshot. I initiated a secure export; assuming Legal sign-off on the transfer agreement we can push the package to Acme's SFTP within ~16 hours. Querylytics artifacts (metrics/aggregates) will require a separate request and may take another 12–24 hours to package due to aggregation jobs.

I'll hold the export pending explicit approval from Acme and sign-off from Legal on the transfer parameters. If we get a DocuSign access agreement today I can kick off the transfer tonight.

— Aditya
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Michael Reynolds <m.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Cc: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-03T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — request for notification timeline and evidence transfer

Michael — appreciate the patience. Internal legal has reviewed and proposed a short transfer addendum to the DPA to cover temporary evidence exports (see attached redlines). Key points:

- Redwood will provide initial incident notice within 24 hours of verification for customers with regulated-data clauses; otherwise within 48 hours.
- Evidence exports to customer-managed endpoints require: (a) a written access agreement (we can use DocuSign), (b) MD5 checksums and manifest from Redwood, and (c) a one-time SFTP account tied to the transfer window.
- If evidence includes third-party subprocessor data, Redwood will coordinate but cannot unilaterally compel subprocessor-provided artifacts. We'll request their assisted export and pass along ETA.

Please confirm: (1) whether Acme can sign the access addendum via DocuSign today, and (2) the SFTP host/path you'd like us to push the package to. Once we have that we'll schedule the export and provide a signed transfer manifest.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dpa_section4_redlines.docx (docx, 54 KB); transfer_addendum_v1.pdf (pdf, 22 KB)
